control_name: Cross-Origin Request Restriction (Reverse Proxy Origin Enforcement)
description: Configure the reverse proxy or load balancer (nginx, Apache httpd, HAProxy) to validate the Origin and Referer headers on state-changing requests (POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, and WebSocket Upgrade) against an explicit allowlist of trusted origins. Requests with an Origin that does not match the allowlist are rejected with 403 before reaching the backend application. This provides defense-in-depth for applications that fail to validate cross-origin requests internally — the proxy enforces the same-origin boundary at the infrastructure layer.

cvss_vector_impacts.rationale: The attacker must achieve a same-origin position (e.g., XSS on the allowed domain or social engineering to access a same-origin page) to bypass the proxy-level origin restriction. A simple cross-origin request from an attacker-controlled domain is rejected by the proxy before reaching the application, significantly increasing the complexity required for successful exploitation.

verification.method: Check reverse proxy configuration for Origin/Referer header validation on state-changing requests. The proxy should reject requests with an Origin not in the trusted allowlist.

commands.expected: Non-empty output — nginx origin validation map or valid_referers directive found
Non-empty output — Apache Origin validation rules found
Non-empty output — HAProxy Origin ACL rules found

remediation.name: nginx Origin header allowlist with map-based rejection

steps.description: Create an nginx map that validates the Origin header against an explicit allowlist of trusted origins (replace <trusted_origin> entries with your actual origins, e.g., https://app.example.com)
Test nginx configuration for syntax errors
Reload nginx to apply the origin restriction rules

remediation.name: Apache httpd Origin header enforcement via SetEnvIf and Require

steps.description: Create an Apache config drop-in that rejects POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH requests from untrusted origins (replace <trusted_origin> with your actual origin, e.g., https://app.example.com)
steps.command:
printf '<IfModule mod_setenvif.c>
    SetEnvIf Origin "^https://<trusted_origin>$" ORIGIN_OK=1
    SetEnvIf Origin "^https://<trusted_origin_2>$" ORIGIN_OK=1
</IfModule>

<Location />
    <If "%%{REQUEST_METHOD} in { \x27POST\x27, \x27PUT\x27, \x27DELETE\x27, \x27PATCH\x27 }">
        <RequireAll>
            Require all granted
            Require env ORIGIN_OK
        </RequireAll>
    </If>
</Location>
' > /etc/httpd/conf.d/cme-915-origin-restrict.conf

steps.description: Test Apache configuration for syntax errors
Reload Apache to apply the origin restriction rules

remediation.name: HAProxy Origin header ACL with deny on mismatch

steps.description: Add Origin ACL rules to the HAProxy frontend config (replace <trusted_origin> with your actual origins). Add these lines to the appropriate frontend section in /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg
steps.command:
printf '
# CME-915: Cross-Origin Request Restriction
acl is_state_changing method POST PUT DELETE PATCH
acl origin_present req.hdr(Origin) -m found
acl origin_allowed req.hdr(Origin) -m str https://<trusted_origin> https://<trusted_origin_2>
http-request deny deny_status 403 if is_state_changing origin_present !origin_allowed
' >> /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg

steps.description: Reload HAProxy to apply the origin restriction ACLs
